translation: The disease of malaria (nue) erupts from summerheat in most cases. Although the formularies distinguish phlegm, food, cold, heat, and miasmic malaria, malaria in young children mostly arises from disease of the spleen and stomach.

However, the qi is timid and the spirit clouded, so at the onset fright epilepsy and reversal are common. In summer and autumn one must never take it for fright epilepsy. In adult malaria, one must distinguish the twelve channels, just as in cough. In pediatrics, vulgar physicians only remove ginseng from Xiao Chaihu Tang, or use Xiangru and Gegen. Not knowing that Chaihu robs the liver yin and Gegen exhausts the stomach fluids, they repeatedly cause transformations.

Young children are pure yang, and summerheat is hot qi. The pattern must have much heat with vexation and thirst; for those whose pathogen is received through the lung, two doses of Guizhi Baihu Tang will surely cure.
